title: Manyhands JSON v1 synchronization conflict
description: What conflict show reads of a remote synchronization's conflict: where it stands, what it needs next, and, while it is live, its observation and each conflicted path. A requested read: the sides are content. Nothing is written by the read.

operation_id.description: The synchronization's ID, whichever ID was asked for: the synchronization's own, or the operation of a comment it publishes.

comment_operation_id.description: The operation of the comment the synchronization publishes, or null when it publishes none.

target.description: The branch the synchronization synchronizes: primary, or a document's or a ticket's editing branch.

item_id.description: The item whose editing branch it synchronizes, or null for primary.

stage.description: The merge the conflict is in: the item's remote branch into its editing branch (context), or primary into the branch (primary).

next_action.description: What the conflict needs next. resolve only when the set is not empty and every path is eligible canonical content; external_repair when the merge is finished in Git outside Manyhands; retry_resolution when the request named by request_id may continue its attempt; resume when operation resume finishes the operation; synchronize when a new synchronization publishes what a cancelled one left; none once it is published.

request_id.description: The request whose resolution attempt is unfinished, or null.

eligibility.description: Whether the live conflict's set can be resolved in Manyhands, one value for the whole set; null when no conflict is live.

local_parent.description: The commit the merge began from on the local branch.

incoming_parent.description: The commit the merge took in.

observation.description: conflict-v1: and a digest of the live conflict, which a resolution presents; null when no conflict is live. It is re-derived on every read and is valid only while the conflict is unchanged.

historical.description: True when a resolution attempt has written paths: the sides are the recorded conflict's, and the worktree may already hold results.

paths.description: The live conflict's paths, ordered by raw path bytes; empty when no conflict is live.
